note: Brook's sprites. Files live in art/in/ (paths below are relative to art/). Names are the strip names; the M4 renderer still draws placeholder rects (art is wired in M6). Strips are horizontal, frame 00 on the left; pivot bottom-centre unless given.

sprites.name: lark-turnaround
sprites.note: Reference sheet, not an engine strip. Shows rope tail and hook because section 6 asks for them. Throat painted in key greens.

sprites.name: lark-idle
sprites.note: Faces right. Body only, no rope drawn. OPEN: the turnaround and cloak-open frames draw the rope coiled at the feet, and the engine also draws a trailing rope from tailAnchor (just under the back hem point). Vegapunk to decide which one shows. fps 8 is the guide's figure for the 6-frame polish idle; with only these 2 MVP frames, ~2 fps (or holds of ~4 ticks at 8 fps) is suggested.

sprites.name: lark-run
sprites.note: v5 (Nov 3, 2026, approved by Azzato). Faces right, 48x48 cells (384x48 strip), pivot [32,47] (was 32x48 / [16,47]: 16 px of padding on the left for the cloak and rope trailing behind). Jog/run loop for 100 px/s at 16 fps, 6.25 px/frame; frames 3 and 7 are flight frames. The flapping scalloped cloak AND the rope-loop tail are painted into every frame (the rope hangs from the belt between the far-side lining and the near dark panel), so the engine must NOT draw its own cloak swing or rope tail on lark-run (no tailAnchor). Throat in key greens (48 px). Playback stays tied to her actual speed: 16 fps at exactly 100 px/s, scale fps by |vx|/100.

sprites.name: tiles-harbor
sprites.note: Tiles anchor top-left. Window panes in window_* (unlit) are transparent so the sky parallax shows through.

sprites.name: lamp
sprites.note: Hanging/wall prop: pivot is the wall-plate attach point. Flame centre at (15,20) for the light-pool origin.

sprites.name: guard-watchman
sprites.note: Faces right. lightOrigin = flashlight lens, 28 px above the feet (cone origin). Search frames aim the lens 5 px up / 4 px down. '!' frame is the startled pose only; the '!' glyph is UI. Walk contact frames (00, 03) dip 1 px, so the lens sits at y 20 there.

sprites.name: lark-cloak-open
sprites.note: Faces right. Start of the grapple-fire animation. Pass 3 = Azzato's draw-over: frames 00-01 have the rope coiled at the feet, and in frame 02 the rope runs from the gun down through the lifted cloak. Lining is WL1 with WL0 shade, against the black WK1 bodysuit. muzzle = front face of the gun body on frame 02; his hook prongs went 2 px past the frame and are clipped. OPEN: rope drawn on the body vs the engine's trailing rope. Play once and hold frame 02 until the shot. fps 12 is a suggestion. Oct 28 2026 10:45 PM CT: Brook's 8x scale-down of the drawover moved the figure -1/-2/-4 px in frames 0/1/2 (measured: exact alpha match at those shifts) and un-clipped the hook, so tailAnchor is per frame and muzzle (gun front face, frame 2) is [27,21] (was [31,21]).

sprites.name: lark-gun-out
sprites.note: Faces right. The two gun-out poses at 48x48 with Azzato's full, unclipped grapple hook. Frame 00 = turnaround side view; frame 01 = cloak-open frame 02. Each is the pass-3 32x48 frame padded 8 px left and right, so its (16,47) pivot lands on (24,47), and with the 2 hook-prong columns restored at x40-41. Same palette, throat key greens and WL1/WL0 lining as pass 3. muzzle is per frame [x,y] in 48x48 coordinates: the hook tip column (x41) on the barrel's centre row, between the two prongs. tailAnchor = the 32-px [11,40] + 8 x. The 32-px turnaround and cloak-open strips are unchanged; Vegapunk decides how this strip replaces or overlays them.

sprites.name: lark-idle-bell
sprites.note: Standing bell-belly idle (Azzato approved Nov 3): cloak breathes/sways, scalloped hem, rope loop hangs nearly straight from the belt under the hem and sways with the cloak. Painted in, so no engine cloak or rope tail. Throat key greens (24 px). lark-idle.png is unchanged and still exists.

sprites.name: lark-swing
sprites.note: Pass 4. Pendulum poses drawn at their angle (engine does not rotate). angleDeg = grip->body from straight down, + = body right of grip. grip[i] = gun-nose pixel (SL5) where the rope leaves. Poncho painted per pose; ownsCloak[i]=true means the whole streaming/spread poncho is in the frame, so skip the engine cloak tail on that frame. tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured). Pass 5: frames 6-7 (back-90, front-90) are polish frames for the full-extension stall, rope horizontal; poncho spread with the lavender back-half lining behind the legs.

sprites.name: lark-air
sprites.note: release (straight line, cloak tight), rise (legs trailing, cloak dragged down), fall (poncho halves thrown up as wings, legs reaching down), spread (pass 5: optional held/dramatic version of fall, wings wider and flung higher, lavender back-half lining behind the legs). Release stays 1 frame; no tumble. Bottom-aligned to the pivot row. tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured).

sprites.name: lark-freefall
sprites.note: Head-down dive, poncho streaming up and spread; 3-frame flutter (play 0,1,2,1). Pass 5 repaint: the poncho is one piece split only at the centre-front seam, so the inside of the back half (lining, WL1 with WL0 folds) shows behind the legs; hood re-lit so light comes from above in the final head-down orientation. tailAnchor here is the top-back corner of the streaming poncho. tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured).

sprites.name: lark-yank
sprites.note: snap (rope taut, both arms straight to the hook, knees braced, poncho flaring away) then launch (stretched line past the anchor, poncho streaming). grip[i] = gun nose (SL5). tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured).

sprites.name: lark-roll
sprites.note: Landing roll: land-tuck, ball (~-110 deg), ball (~-220 deg), kneel-rise. Bottom-aligned to the pivot row; poncho wrapped, engine tail allowed. tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured).

sprites.name: lark-ledge
sprites.note: Ledge grab + pull-up: reach, hang, pull-up (knee hooked on lip), crouch-top. ledgeHand[i] = the frame pixel that should sit on the ledge lip corner (hand for 0-2, front toe for 3); align the frame so that pixel lands on the lip. Frames are bbox-centred, not pivot-locked. tailAnchor = one pixel past the back-most hem point of the painted poncho (auto-measured).

mock.note: Style target, not a game asset. Composite with engine-style lighting, so off-palette pixels are expected.
